outcome.label: Outcome:
outcome.sentNote: Sent means the mail server accepted the message, not necessarily that it reached the inbox. The system cannot see messages that land in spam or are blocked on the receiving side.
outcome.unknownNote: It is unclear whether the message went out — the mail server did not respond in time. The system does not resend automatically, so the recipient never gets it twice. To resend, the app service sends a new request.
outcome.recipientGone: no longer in the recipient list
outcome.whyBlocked: To see why this person was blocked: open <link>the page of <mono>{id}</mono></link>. Settings there are current, not as of sending.

errorCodes.byCodeTitle: Read errors by <mono>code</mono>, not by wording
errorCodes.byCodeBody: Every error is <mono>application/problem+json</mono>. For <mono>422</mono>, the outer <mono>code</mono> is just <mono>VALIDATION</mono> — the specific code is in <mono>issues[].code</mono>, with <mono>path</mono> pointing to the wrong field.
errorCodes.retryBody: <mono>4xx</mono>: do not retry unchanged — it will fail the same way. <mono>5xx</mono> and timeouts: retry with backoff, keeping the same <mono>idempotencyKey</mono> field in the body — the same key never sends twice. The MVP does not return <mono>429</mono> yet.
errorCodes.acceptedBody: The email goes out later, from the queue. Track it with <mono>GET /v1/notifications/:id</mono>. Even <mono>sent</mono> only means the mail server accepted it, not necessarily that it reached the inbox.

templateIssues.VARIABLE_MISSING_SOURCE: Variable has no source — write '{{ payload.… }}' or '{{ user.… }}'.
templateIssues.VARIABLE_NOT_IN_SCHEMA: The variable is used in the content but not declared in the variable table.

templateIssues.FOOTER_NOT_ALLOWED: Do not write '{{ footer }}' yourself — the system inserts the footer.
templateIssues.UNSUBSCRIBE_LINK_NOT_ALLOWED: Do not write an unsubscribe link yourself (not even the word "unsubscribe") — the system inserts it.
templateIssues.LINK_SCHEME_NOT_ALLOWED: Links must be https:// or mailto: only.
templateIssues.USER_VARIABLE_NOT_SUPPORTED: This user.* variable is not supported yet — only '{{ user.external_id }}' exists.

templateIssues.VERSION_SUPERSEDED: This version has been superseded — create a new draft instead of republishing.
templateIssues.IMAGE_URL_NOT_ALLOWED: Image links must be https:// and contain no variables.
templateIssues.DESIGN_TOO_LARGE: The design is too large. Shorten text or HTML blocks.
templateIssues.HTML_TAG_NOT_ALLOWED: The email contains a tag that is not allowed in email (e.g. script, iframe, form). Remove it and save again.
templateIssues.HTML_ATTRIBUTE_NOT_ALLOWED: The email contains an unsafe attribute (e.g. onclick, onerror). Remove it and save again.
templateIssues.HTML_URL_NOT_ALLOWED: There is an unsafe link (e.g. javascript:). Links may only be https://, mailto: or a variable.
templateIssues.HTML_STYLE_NOT_ALLOWED: A style contains something that is not allowed (e.g. external fonts, code in CSS).
templateIssues.HTML_MALFORMED: The email content is broken and cannot be read (an unclosed tag, quote or comment). Fix or undo it and save again.
templateIssues.HTML_TOO_LARGE: The email is too large (max 256 KB). Remove some content.

webhooks.title: Webhooks
webhooks.subtitle: EWS reports delivery results to {app}'s URL
webhooks.notConfiguredTitle: Webhooks are not enabled on the server
webhooks.notConfiguredBody: The EWS server has no webhook signing key (WEBHOOK_SIGNING_KEY), so URLs cannot be added, secrets rotated or tests sent yet. Contact the EWS operators.
webhooks.intro: Whenever an email has an outcome (sent, failed, blocked) or is opened, EWS POSTs to the registered URL — the app does not have to keep polling.
webhooks.emptyBody: {app} has not registered for webhooks. Add a URL so EWS reports delivery results.
webhooks.howCall: A POST with a JSON body carrying the event id, event type and the email's outcome. Respond with 2xx within 10 seconds.
webhooks.howSignature: Every call carries <mono>X-EWS-Signature: t=…,v1=…</mono> — verify it with the secret before trusting the body (integration guide, section 7).
webhooks.howRetry: If the app fails or does not answer, EWS retries after 1 min · 5 min · 30 min · 2 h · 6 h, then stops (6 calls in total).
webhooks.howDuplicate: The same event may arrive twice — drop duplicates by <mono>id</mono>.
webhooks.howPrivacy: The body contains no email address and no email content.
webhooks.addBody: The URL must be https:// and reachable from the internet. URLs pointing into a private network are rejected. The secret is shown once right after adding.
webhooks.editBody: Choose which events this URL receives. To change the URL, delete it and add a new one.
webhooks.eventSent: The mail server accepted the email
webhooks.eventFailed: The email could not be sent
webhooks.eventNoRecipient: Not sent because the recipient is blocked (topic off, email unsubscribed…)
webhooks.eventOpened: The recipient opened the email for the first time (needs Open tracking on)
webhooks.disableBody: EWS stops calling this URL. Calls waiting for a retry are cancelled — enabling it again does NOT replay old events.
webhooks.rotateBody: The old secret stops working on the NEXT call — the app must switch to the new secret or it will reject every call. The new secret is shown only once.
webhooks.deleteBody: EWS stops calling this URL; pending calls and the call log are deleted. This cannot be undone.
webhooks.secretBody: The secret is shown ONCE. Copy it into the app's configuration — after closing it cannot be shown again, only rotated.
webhooks.secretUsage: The app uses this secret to verify the <mono>X-EWS-Signature</mono> header of every call from EWS.
webhooks.secretSaved: I have stored the secret somewhere safe
webhooks.secretConfirmBody: After closing, this secret cannot be shown again. To get one you will have to rotate it.
webhooks.hintBlocked: The URL points to a private network address — EWS does not call there.
webhooks.hintTimeout: The app did not answer within 10 seconds.
webhooks.hintConnection: Could not connect to the URL (wrong domain, server down, broken HTTPS certificate…).
webhooks.hintHttp: The app answered with a non-2xx code. Check the webhook route and the signature check.
webhooks.hintOther: See the error code next to it.
webhooks.deliveriesEmpty: No calls yet. Send an email, or use Send test.
webhooks.pageSubtitle: Both directions for {app}: EWS reports results to the app, and external tools call in to publish

limits.title: Sending limits
limits.subtitle: App {app}
limits.windowHint: Send only on the chosen days and hours. Emails arriving outside the window are held and go out when it opens.
limits.daysDef: Days of the week when emails may be sent.
limits.hoursDef: Hours of the day when emails may be sent, Vietnam time.
limits.windowMandatoryDef: On: mandatory messages go out right away, even outside the window.
limits.pacingHint: Limits how many emails go out each minute. Emails over the limit move to the following minutes instead of going out at once.
limits.perMinuteDef: The most emails the app sends in one minute.
limits.pacingMandatoryDef: On: mandatory messages do not wait and go before regular emails.
limits.ceilingHint: The most emails the app may send per minute, for every email including mandatory ones. Set by Super Admin only.
limits.ceilingDef: "Emails per minute" under Pacing cannot exceed this number.
limits.errTime: Start time must be before end time
limits.errNumber: Enter a whole number from 1 to {max}

incoming.notConfigured: Webhooks are not enabled on the server.
incoming.needTopicAndTemplate: Needs an active topic and a published template.
incoming.emptyBody: Add a webhook so another system can send notifications through EWS.

incoming.deleteBody: The URL stops working immediately. This cannot be undone.

systemSettings.title: System settings
systemSettings.subtitle: Operational numbers for every app — no deploy needed
systemSettings.incomingIntro: Applies to every /hooks/… URL of every app.
systemSettings.dedupeHelp: When a call has no dedupe key, identical content within this window publishes only once.
systemSettings.rateHelp: Above this the tool gets 429 — stops an alert storm from sending a flood of emails.
systemSettings.baseUrlHelp: The domain external tools call (through NPM). The console builds full hook URLs from it. Empty = only the /hooks/… part is shown.
systemSettings.outOfRange: Enter a whole number from {min} to {max}.
systemSettings.propagation: New values take effect on every API server within 30 seconds.
systemSettings.maxKeysLabel: Maximum active API keys per app
systemSettings.maxKeysHelp: At this number a key must be revoked before another is issued.
systemSettings.maxHooksHelp: At this number a hook must be deleted before another is added.
systemSettings.maxEndpointsHelp: Each URL adds one call for every email that finishes. At this number a URL must be deleted before another is added.
systemSettings.htmlCheckHelp: When on, HTML templates cannot be published if they contain runnable code (script, onclick…), javascript: links, non-https:// images or broken HTML — same as Visual templates. Published versions are not affected. Off = publish as before.
systemSettings.lockoutEnabledHelp: When on, exceeding the number of wrong passwords below locks sign-in temporarily. Off = no counting, no locking (accounts already locked stay locked). Microsoft sign-in is never temporarily locked.
systemSettings.maxFailedHelp: This many failures for the same email (within the window below) locks that email temporarily — including emails that do not exist.
systemSettings.failureWindowHelp: Counted from the first failure; if the window ends before the limit, counting starts over.
systemSettings.lockoutMinutesHelp: The lock lifts by itself after this time. A Super Admin can lift it earlier in the table below.
systemSettings.ipMaxFailedHelp: All emails signing in from one IP added together — stops trying one password against many emails. If the office shares one public IP, set this high so the whole office is not locked out.
systemSettings.permanentAfterLabel: Lock permanently after consecutive temporary locks
systemSettings.permanentAfterHelp: After this many temporary locks in a row (within 24 hours, with no successful sign-in) the account is locked for good: only a Super Admin can unlock it, open sessions are signed out and Microsoft sign-in is blocked too. 0 = never — keep 0 unless needed, since anyone who knows an email can lock that person out on purpose.

security.title: Monitoring & Security
security.subtitle: Blocking repeated failed password sign-ins, and the locks currently held
security.rulesIntro: Applies to password sign-in on the console. A locked person only sees "incorrect email or password" — they are not told they are locked.
security.locksIntro: Temporary locks lift by themselves; permanent locks can only be lifted here. Unlocking an email also clears its failure counter.
security.loadFailed: Could not load the lock list
security.emptyHint: When someone enters a wrong password too many times, the lock shows up here.
security.unlockEmail: Removes the lock and clears the failure counter for this email. They can sign in again right away.
security.unlockAccount: This account is permanently locked. Unlocking lets them sign in right away — only do it once you are sure it is really them (for example, after calling them).
security.unlockIp: Removes the lock on this IP. Everyone signing in from it can try again right away.
security.notFound: This lock just expired or someone already lifted it. The list has been reloaded.
security.cliHint: If the Super Admin is the one locked out: run <cmd>admin-cli unlock-login --email …</cmd> in the api container.
security.rulesSummaryOn: On · {max} failures within {window} minutes lock for {lock} minutes · {ip} failures from one IP lock that IP · permanent lock: {permanent}
security.rulesSummaryOff: Off — failures are not counted, nothing is locked
security.permanentAfter: after {count} temporary locks in a row

appTransition.suspendBody: The app stops sending immediately. API keys remain; resuming picks up where it left off — nothing is lost.
appTransition.resumeBody: The app can send again right away. Permissions and API keys stay as they were before suspension.
appTransition.revokeBody: Revoked is a FINAL state — there is no way back, not even resume. The app stops sending permanently. Suspend instead if you might use it again.
appTransition.reasonPlaceholder: The team has ended the project and no longer sends notifications.
appTransition.reasonHint: Required; goes into the system log. Up to 500 characters.

grant.unenforced: These two numbers are currently stored but not enforced — an app over the limit is not rejected. Per-app quota is planned in section 12.5.
grant.ack: This team already has a «Notification settings» screen for employees. Without it, employees have no way to opt out.

wizard.pageSubtitle: Create a new publisher for EWS Notification Service
wizard.profileDraftNote: The app is <mono>active</mono> as soon as it is created and can send email right away — no review.
wizard.namespaceNote: The namespace is the app’s ownership within the organization; only one app per organization holds it. Treat it as fixed once set.
wizard.originNote: Internal = a service inside the company network. External = called from outside.
wizard.grantLater: The sending channel granted by default is email. You get the API key in step 4.
wizard.topicsDraftNote: Topics are created as <mono>draft</mono>; activate them on the Topics screen before sending.
wizard.topicKeyRule: Lowercase letters, digits and <mono>_ . -</mono>, starting with a letter, 2–128 characters.
wizard.topicKeyDuplicate: This key is already used by another topic.
wizard.defaultMode: Default when the user has not chosen
wizard.optIn: opt_in — does NOT receive by default
wizard.mandatoryHint: Users cannot turn it off. Only for messages they must receive, e.g. unusual sign-in alerts — still never sent to broken or unsubscribed addresses.
wizard.reviewNote: Creating registers the app in the system and issues its first API key.
wizard.stoppedTitle: The app was created, but stopped at step «{step}»
wizard.stoppedBody: {message} The app was created and is <mono>active</mono> — do not create it again (the slug would clash); <link>open the app</link> to finish.
wizard.activeNote: The app is active. The new topics are still <mono>draft</mono> — go to <link>Topics</link> and activate them before the app can send.
